mustFix.title: Decision-type limb asserts the no-cell-edit branch runs 'D-170 through D-237', which absorbs the cell-editing decision D-236 into that branch and contradicts the immediately preceding adopted entry's own measurement of the same range
mustFix.where: docs/coop/artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-238.draft.md lines 9-10, '(0 blockers, 0 SHOULD-FIX). Same no-cell-edit branch as D-170 through D-237.'
mustFix.claimUnderTest: That every decision from D-170 through D-237 inclusive sits on the same no-cell-edit branch.
mustFix.evidence: D-236 edits file 08 cells. Git is dispositive: commit fc688b1 ('D-236: record DR-104 SATISFIED under D-056 Class B') modifies docs/v2/architecture/08-decision-and-readiness-register.md with 3 insertions and 3 deletions; `git log -- docs/v2/architecture/08-decision-and-readiness-register.md` lists fc688b1 as the most recent file-08 commit. D-236's own operative text directs those cell rewrites: it replaces the unique DR-104 lead prefix, rewrites condition 2 to '5 of 32 SATISFIED, standing NOT MET', and rewrites the one-sentence summary; its narrowing instruction is 'Do not edit gate-harness cells', which concedes that non-gate-harness cells were edited. By contrast D-237 (commit 0a814f9) touches no file-08 path at all.
mustFix.precedentEvidence: The house convention for this limb is a contiguous range ending at the immediate predecessor: D-230 'through D-229', D-231 'through D-230', D-232 'through D-231', D-233 'through D-232', D-234 'through D-233', D-235 'through D-234'. D-237 breaks that +1 pattern and writes 'D-170 through D-235', stopping exactly one short of its own predecessor. That break is not a slip: it is the deliberate exclusion of D-236, and it appears identically in both the adopted D-237 COORD entry and the frozen D-237 draft, having survived the same three-turn dual adversarial protocol. D-236 itself carries no 'no-cell-edit branch' sentence, because it is not on that branch.
mustFix.whyItMatters: This is a false provenance claim in a limb of a COORD entry that is destined for permanent append-only adoption. It silently re-characterizes an adopted SATISFIED cell-editing decision as a no-cell-edit recording, and it overwrites, without argument, a range boundary that the immediately preceding entry established under review. The draft is elsewhere accurate about D-236's effects, correctly reporting 'Condition 2 stays 5 of 32' (the value D-236 wrote) and correctly listing D-236 in the Reversibility 'does not unwrite' set, so the defect is a localized misstatement of the branch boundary rather than a misreading of D-236 throughout, and it repairs cleanly.
mustFix.scopeOfViolation: D-236 is the only decision in D-170..D-237 that touches file 08; the file-08 commits immediately prior are 892236a (D-169), 1dcff76 (D-167) and 0fcf3d3 (D-158), all outside the range's D-170 floor. D-170 through D-235 is therefore genuinely clean, which is precisely why D-237's boundary was correct.
mustFix.suggestedRepair: Restore the exclusion of D-236. Either 'Same no-cell-edit branch as D-170 through D-235, and D-237.' or 'Same no-cell-edit branch as D-237.' Do not write a range that spans D-236. This repair touches only the subject draft's decision-type limb; it requires no change to file 08, to COORD, to leftover-join v7, or to any Stage A verdict, and it has no scope effect.

decision: OBJECT. The subject is unmoved at the dispatched digest and mode 0444, HEAD and last live heading match, all ten cited digests recompute correctly, both Stage A verdicts are ACCEPT 0/0 at mode 0444, the Stage A observation-honesty clause is present and exact, the per-platform scoping claim re-derives correctly from corpus v3, input-corpus v1 and occupancy v2 primary bytes, and every prohibition on the dispatch attack list is clean. One MUST-FIX lands outside that list. The decision-type limb claims the no-cell-edit branch runs 'D-170 through D-237', but D-236 edits file 08 cells: commit fc688b1 changes the register by 3 insertions and 3 deletions, and D-236's operative text directs those rewrites while narrowing only to 'Do not edit gate-harness cells'. The house convention is a contiguous range ending at the immediate predecessor (D-233 through D-232, D-234 through D-233, D-235 through D-234), and D-237 deliberately broke that pattern to write 'D-170 through D-235', excluding D-236; that exclusion survived D-237's own three-turn dual adversarial protocol in both the draft and the adopted entry. Absorbing D-236 back into the branch is a false provenance claim in an entry destined for permanent adoption. The repair is confined to one sentence in the subject and has no scope effect.
